title: Phoenix
subtitle: An ember-winged stretch above basalt.
interpretation: A living firebird settles from a wing stretch, supported by a firm grip on a basalt ledge.
gesture: One wing rises while the other opens outward; the lifted breast and swept tail hold an asymmetric, alert balance.
polish: Preserve unequal wing planes, tapered breast, long flight feathers and tail sweep.
Bury feather roots under thin fitted coverts that follow the flight planes.
Keep the ankle, toes and keratin tips visibly connected around the basalt ledge.
nativeFeatures: Editable native meshes with selectively rebuilt lower-wing coverts and fitted digits
Fitted Fan lift control carries lower-wing mantle, coverts, secondary vanes and shafts, wrist and primary fan
Armature, skin weights and rigid wing/feather hierarchy
reference: Preserves the procedural Phoenix body, face, outer flight vanes, shafts and asymmetric gesture, with selective native reconstruction of lower-wing coverage and fitted grip. Imported triangulated meshes remain editable; original procedural recipes and quad topology are not recovered.
reviewStatus: Regional wing and grip reconstruction; publication scope and parent observations belong to its immutable review.
